# research

For questions the codebase can't answer: what a library does, what an
API supports, what a spec says. A delegated agent does the reading so
the main session's context stays lean; a durable answer lands as a
note in `research/` at the repo root.

Codebase questions are not research — they belong to in-loop or
rubberduck's research phase. A foreign product installed on the
machine is: `~/.codex`, a vendor's binary, a tool's own bundled files
are primary sources about that product, not this repo's code.

## The main session doesn't gather

Delegating and then reading around the edges defeats the point. The
main session writes the question, spawns, and works from what comes
back. It never fetches a page, runs a command against an outside
install, or greps a foreign tool's files — not before the spawn to
check something quickly first, and not after to double-check the
answer. What it may read: the agent's note, and files in this repo.

That quick check beforehand is the failure mode this rule exists for.
It costs more context than the agent it was meant to save, and a
partial look is how you get to a confident wrong answer.

## Ask, or just go

Taking up a new topic is a *what* — offer it, the user's yes starts
it. Getting information the running task already needs is a *how* —
delegate it without asking. The alternative to spawning is not
skipping the work; it is the main session doing it badly.

## Before spawning

Check `research/` for an existing note on the topic. One that answers
the question → report it, done. Outdated or partial → the agent
updates that file (new checked-date) instead of creating a sibling.

## The agent

One agent per question; several questions run as parallel agents, one
file each. Run it in the background where the harness supports it —
the session keeps working meanwhile — otherwise as a plain subagent.
Pick a cheaper model where the harness allows it: mid-tier, not
bottom-tier — tracing claims to their sources takes judgment. Claude
Code and Codex take a model on the spawn call. Cursor has the same
knob but undocumented and unreliable, so ask for the model and accept
whatever it gives you (`research/subagent-model-selection.md`).

The agent's job:

1. Investigate against **primary sources** — official docs, source
   code, specs, changelogs, first-party APIs, a vendor's own installed
   files — never a secondary write-up of them. Follow every claim back
   to the source that owns it. What can't be confirmed is said so in
   the answer, never guessed.
2. Quote the source verbatim for the claim the answer rests on, and
   for anything that contradicts a decision already in force. A
   summariser's paraphrase of a page is weaker evidence than the line
   itself, and the note should show which one it has.

## Note, or just an answer

An answer is durable when it changes a decision, belongs in PLAN.md,
or saves a future session the same work — that one gets a note. A
one-off fact is relayed in chat and dies there, so `research/` stays
small enough that the check above is worth doing. Decide at spawn; if
a fact turns out to weigh more than expected, ask the agent for the
note afterwards.

## Note shape

```markdown
# <Title>

Checked <YYYY-MM-DD>, primary sources. Question: <as posed>.

**<The answer, up front.>**

<Findings, with a source URL per claim.>
```

No YAML frontmatter. One file per question, at
`research/<kebab-topic>.md` — no date in the filename, so other docs
can keep referencing it.

## When the answer looks wrong

Split by the kind of doubt. "Is this precise?" goes back to the same
agent — it still has its sources and its context. "Did you make this
up?" goes to a fresh agent that never saw the first answer, because
independence is the entire point of asking twice. Either way it is an
agent; the main session does not go and look for itself.

## Done

Relay the file path and the TL;DR. Never commit — that's the user's
call. If the question served a ticket discussion, offer to fold the
conclusion into the ticket via the tickets gate (or the running
rubberduck flow) — no automatic coupling.

## Boundary

- Codebase questions → in-loop / rubberduck; a foreign product's own
  files → here
- The main session never gathers, before or after the spawn
- Never commits, never touches Jira
- Notes in English, chat in the user's language — as always
